content.title: Terms describing various indications for mechanical circulatory support

indications.description: Use of MCS (LVAD, BiVAD or TAH) to keep a patient alive who is otherwise at high risk of death before transplantation until a donor organ becomes available.
Use of MCS (short-term or long-term) to keep a patient alive until cardiac function recovers sufficiently to remove MCS.
Long-term use of MCS (LVAD) as an alternative to transplantation in patients with end-stage HF ineligible for transplantation.

indications.term: Bridge to decision / Bridge to bridge
indications.description: Use of short-term MCS (ECMO or Impella) in patients with cardiogenic shock until haemodynamics and end-organ perfusion are stabilized, contraindications for long-term MCS are excluded (e.g., brain damage after resuscitation) and additional therapeutic options including long-term VAD therapy or heart transplant can be evaluated.
Use of MCS (usually LVAD) to improve end-organ function and/or to make an ineligible patient eligible for heart transplantation.

abbreviations.Impella: percutaneous ventricular assist device (mentioned as an example of short-term MCS)

content.source_notes: Content corresponds to Table 15 and accompanying explanatory text describing indications for mechanical circulatory support; entries appear twice on the page (duplicate table).
